newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslav socially-owned capital value rises - IEN.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslav socially-owned capital value rises - IEN.

text.p: Yugoslavia increased by 28 billion German marks the value of the socially-owned capital in 1996 to be privatised under the new ownership transformation law, a Belgrade think-tank said on Tuesday.

"After revaluation at the end of last year, the value of socially-owned property to be privatised increased by 28 billion German marks," said Stojan Stamenkovic, leading economist of the Institute for Economic Sciences (IEN).
Revaluation of assets is based on retail price growth and dinar exchange rate is used as a base for revaluation of the country's liabilities, which also include its foreign debt, he said.
The average price increase in 1996 was 93 percent on the previous year while the dinar rate remained stable at 3.3 dinars to the German mark.
"It is one of the paradoxes of the economy here -- the real value of gross domestic product falls, losses rise, but the value of the socially-owned property increases," Stamenkovic said.
"But the market will set the real value of the companies after their privatisation," he added.
Serbian parliament currently in session is expected to adopt its first privatisation law in coming days.
Some 5,000 firms worth an estimated 100 billion German marks are seen privatising under the law, 80 percent of which within the first two years. -- Gordana Kukic, Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 222 4254
